security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and TypeScript template literals. The skill is Azure SDK documentation with expected endpoint, environment variable, and file-upload examples, but the SAS examples should use narrower permissions. No prompt injection or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Change SAS examples to least-privilege permissions and shorter expirations. Avoid account-level all-permission SAS in general guidance.
Add warnings to never log account keys, connection strings, or SAS URLs. Prefer DefaultAzureCredential when possible.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad SAS Permission Examples
semantic_findings.description: The container and account SAS examples grant broad write, delete, list, and account-level permissions for 24 hours. Copying this pattern can create overprivileged storage access in production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly set broad permission strings and 24 hour expirations. This is guidance risk rather than malicious behavior, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Azure Blob Storage code often needs correct SDK patterns, authentication, and transfer methods. This skill provides practical TypeScript and JavaScript examples for common blob workflows.
actual_capabilities: Demonstrates authentication with DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, shared keys, and SAS tokens.
Provides examples for creating, listing, and deleting containers.
Provides examples for uploading, downloading, listing, deleting, and copying blobs.
Covers blob, container, and account SAS token generation patterns.
Summarizes TypeScript types, error handling, blob types, and Node.js versus browser support.
limitations: This is a documentation skill and does not execute Azure operations by itself.
Examples require a valid Azure Storage account, credentials, and installed SDK packages.
It does not validate account permissions, network rules, costs, or production policies.
Some examples only apply to Node.js and are not available in browsers.

use_cases.title: Add Blob Uploads
use_cases.description: Use SDK examples to upload strings, buffers, files, streams, browser files, and binary data to Azure Blob Storage.

use_cases.title: Configure Storage Authentication
use_cases.description: Compare DefaultAzureCredential, connection strings, shared keys, and SAS tokens before choosing an authentication pattern.

use_cases.title: Manage Storage Containers
use_cases.description: Create, list, delete, and organize containers and blobs with examples for common maintenance tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Upload Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple upload path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a TypeScript Azure Blob Storage upload flow for a text file. Use DefaultAzureCredential and explain each required variable.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Authentication Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the right credential pattern for an application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Azure Blob Storage authentication options for my Node.js service. Recommend the safest option for production and explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build Container Maintenance Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Create operational workflows for storage containers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TypeScript routines to list containers, list blobs by prefix, delete stale blobs, and handle Azure Storage errors.

prompt_templates.title: Review SAS Token Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review for delegated access.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Azure Blob Storage SAS token strategy. Focus on least privilege, expiration, browser uploads, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: I need a secure upload path for user documents.
output_examples.output: The response outlines SDK setup, recommended authentication, upload method selection, metadata handling, and security checks before deployment.

output_examples.input: I want temporary browser access to one blob.
output_examples.output: The response explains a short-lived read-only SAS token, server-side token generation, expiration limits, and client usage boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need to troubleshoot container creation errors.
output_examples.output: The response maps common Azure Storage status codes to likely causes and suggests permission, naming, and idempotency checks.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential for production services when Azure identity is available.
Use least-privilege SAS tokens with short expirations and narrow resource scope.
Keep account keys, connection strings, and SAS URLs out of logs and source control.
anti_patterns: Do not use account keys in browser applications.
Do not grant broad SAS permissions when read-only access is enough.
Do not copy file-transfer examples without confirming paths, permissions, and data sensitivity.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK guidance and examples that a developer can adapt in their own project.

faq.question: Which SDK package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers @azure/storage-blob for storage operations and @azure/identity for DefaultAzureCredential authentication.

faq.question: Can it help with browser uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes browser upload patterns and notes which credential methods are not available in browsers.

faq.question: Does it support SAS token guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers blob, container, and account SAS concepts, but production tokens should use least privilege.

faq.question: Can it validate my Azure permissions?
faq.answer: No. You must test permissions in your Azure tenant and follow your organization policies.

faq.question: Is it only for TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. The examples use TypeScript style, but most patterns also apply to JavaScript projects.
